name: Legacy Binder
tagline: Get your affairs in order, kindly and clearly
about: Legacy Binder helps you organise the documents, accounts and wishes your family would need, plan your digital legacy, put your care preferences into your own words, and write the letters that say what paperwork can't.
persona: You are a gentle, organised later-life planning guide: practical, unhurried, matter-of-fact about difficult topics, and clear that legal documents need a qualified professional in your jurisdiction.

onboarding.title: Peace of mind, one folder at a time
onboarding.subtitle: A little context makes every checklist specific to you.
bullets: A 'where everything is' guide for family
Care wishes and letters in your own words

tools.title: What do I need in place?
tools.subtitle: Wills, powers, wishes
tools.prompt: For someone in the profile's country and situation who already has: {done} — a table (Document | Purpose | Typically who prepares it | Priority), a checklist of what's missing in the order to tackle it, steps for the first missing item, and a callout that requirements differ by jurisdiction and a qualified professional should prepare or check legal documents.

tools.title: Where everything is
tools.subtitle: A guide for your family

inputs.label: Describe what you have and where
inputs.placeholder: bank at Nationwide, house deeds in the bureau, pension with Aviva, car log book in the glovebox…

tools.prompt: Organise this into a family guide: {stuff}. A table (Item | Where it is | Who to contact | Reference or account type, never full passwords), a checklist of gaps the user should fill in, and a kv (Where this guide will be kept | Who has been told | Date to review). Add a callout on keeping passwords out of this document and using a password manager's emergency access instead.

tools.title: Digital legacy
tools.subtitle: Accounts, photos, subscriptions

inputs.label: Online accounts & devices
inputs.placeholder: Gmail, Facebook, Amazon Prime, iPhone with all the photos, Netflix, online banking

tools.prompt: Plan a digital legacy for: {accounts}. A table (Account | What happens by default | Legacy setting to switch on | Who should have access), steps to back up photos and important files so family can reach them, a checklist of subscriptions to note for cancelling, and a callout on the legal and privacy side of sharing account access.

tools.title: Letter to my family
tools.subtitle: What paperwork can't say

inputs.label: Kind of letter
options: For a grandchild to open later

inputs.label: Rough thoughts
inputs.placeholder: raised in Leeds; met Joan at the dance hall; proudest of the allotment…

tools.prompt: Draft a '{kind}' letter in the user's voice from: {notes}. A quote with the full letter (300–450 words, warm, specific, no clichés), bullets of 5 questions that might unlock more memories to add, and a kv (Where to keep it | Who to tell it exists | When to revisit it).

tools.title: If I can't speak for myself
tools.subtitle: Care preferences, in your words

inputs.label: What matters to you
inputs.placeholder: want to stay at home as long as possible; no feeding tube; my daughter Sue decides; Catholic priest at the end; music: Ella Fitzgerald

tools.prompt: Turn these into an advance statement of care preferences for the profile's country and household: {prefs}, to be shared with: {share}. A quote with the statement in the first person (250–400 words: where I'd like to be cared for, what a good day looks like, treatments I feel strongly about, who speaks for me, spiritual or cultural needs, comforts like music, food and visitors), a kv (Who speaks for me | Where the copy is kept | Who has been told | Date to review), a checklist of the conversations to have and with whom, and a callout that a statement of wishes is not the same as a legally binding advance decision or power of attorney, which need the proper form for the jurisdiction.

disclaimer: General information only, not legal or financial advice. Laws differ by country and state; have wills, powers of attorney and similar documents prepared or checked by a qualified professional.
